summary: Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall and Franz Bopp, later holding posts at Jena (1811), Erlangen-Nürnberg (1826), and Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Leipzig under Christian Gottlob Heyne, Alexander Hamilton, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, holding posts at Jena (1800), Cologne (1804–1807), and TU Dresden (1828).

Friedrich Schleiermacher was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1790). He later held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1804–1807) and the University of Berlin (~1810–1834).

Friedrich Schrader was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He completed his dissertation under doctoral supervisor Richard Pischel at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg between ~1885 and 1889.

Friedrich Weller worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He earned his Dr. phil. and habilitation at Leipzig University under August Conrady, later serving there as Ordinarius (1928) and chair (1938–1958), and joining the Saxon Academy (1943–1980).

Friedrich Wilhelm worked in Indology and Tibetology, studying at the University of Munich (~1952–1956) under Paul Thieme. He held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1957–1964) and the University of Munich (Privatdozent 1963; Professor 1969–1998).
Friedrich Wilhelm Graf is a scholar in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Augsburg (~1986–1999) and the University of Munich (~1999–2014).

Schelling was a philosopher who studied at Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nürnberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Berlin (1841–1845), and served as president of the Bavarian Academy.
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Karl Foy and Georg von der Gabelentz (~1887–1893).

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg (Dr. phil. 1826–1829). He held academic posts at Halle (~1829–1833), Breslau (1834), Bonn (1839), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann studied Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Bonn (~1827–1832) under Lassen, Schlegel, and others, and Munich (~1832–1836). He held posts at Freising, Munich (1838–1839), and the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising (~1839–1861).

Friedrich Zarncke was a linguistics scholar who studied at Rostock and Leipzig (~1844–1847) under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at the University of Rostock (~1847–1848) and Leipzig University (Rektor 1852; full professor 1858).

Friedrich von Adelung was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology who studied at Leipzig University (1787–1790). He held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), and administrative posts at Vienna (1824) and Utrecht (1825).

Friedrich von Spiegel was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology scholar. He studied at Erlangen, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena under Rückert, Lassen, Fleischer, and Brockhaus, later serving as professor of oriental languages at Erlangen-Nürnberg (1849–1891).

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, studying at Amsterdam, Banaras Hindu University, and Madras. His main posts included SOAS (1958–1962), Amsterdam (1962–1967), and the University of California, Berkeley (1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at the University of Bonn (1934), Munich (1936–1941), and Mainz (~1947–1969).

Frédéric Baudry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian posts at Versailles (1849) and Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1859), and served as administrator of Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885).
Fuguan Xu was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Meiji University (~1928–1931) and under Shili Xiong (~1943–1949), later holding a post at Tunghai University (~1955–1969).
Fujio Oda is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyushu University (~1952–1956). He held academic posts at Fukuoka University (~1976–2004) and Beppu University.
